picks.rationale: Rockstar standing up a dedicated LA team for hand-authored NPC fidelity is the strongest counter-model to the generative-NPC pitch, and it tells designers where the industry's most-watched studio is actually spending craft budget.
picks.excerpt: Rockstar built a dedicated team to push NPC behaviour past Red Dead Redemption 2's 'level of interactive fidelity'. It's a hand-authored, systems-driven answer to the generative-NPC pitch the rest of the industry is selling.

picks.rationale: The most directly actionable item in the pool: game-ready characters with usable topology in under 10 seconds is the exact gap that has kept AI meshes out of production pipelines.
picks.excerpt: Tripo's chief scientist details Smart Mesh, which generates game-ready characters with usable topology in under 10 seconds. The pitch is closing the gap between AI-generated meshes and assets that survive a Maya/Blender production pipeline.

picks.rationale: A leaked DLSS 5 neural-graphics build re-rendering Skyrim and San Andreas is the first live test of AI post-processing overriding an art director's intent — a new authorship problem shipping at driver level.
picks.excerpt: PC players are running leaked DLSS 5 neural graphics over GTA: San Andreas and Skyrim, and the results are photoreal but uncanny. It's an early look at AI re-rendering overriding an art director's original intent.

picks.rationale: Saber's CCO puts the clearest 'prove it with craft' thesis on record from inside a studio already under fire — the argument every AI-using team will be measured against.
picks.excerpt: Saber's chief creative officer argues one genuinely great AI-built game would flip public sentiment overnight. It's the clearest statement yet of the 'prove it with craft' position inside a studio already under fire.

picks.rationale: An id Software founder reframing gen AI as continuous with Doom-era tech culture is a rare, credible counterweight to the 'real devs don't use AI' framing dominating this week's discourse.
picks.excerpt: An id Software co-founder argues the Doom-era team would have grabbed generative tools instantly, framing AI as continuous with the studio's tech-first culture. A useful counterweight to the 'real devs don't use AI' framing.
